cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Make It Official
cards.instruction: Recruit someone by giving them a title, role, or ceremonial duty that makes participation feel binding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Would you be honorary patron of our roof appeal? You'd open it and thank the donors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can come, but I won't make a speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Then accept the patron's ribbon and lead the applause. That can be your ceremonial duty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I leave after the first donation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The patron applauds every donor. We couldn't have the later ones thinking their money mattered less.

mechanism: A recruits its former nervous-speaking pupil as ceremonial patron, adapting speech refusal into applause that binds B to stay for every donor.
confusable: Not making B share blame for a project: the title ceremonial meaning itself prolongs participation.
comparison: Temporary lantern favor made office versus tailored patron duty accepted without speech.
